$comment: Every known zbc consumer. Hand-maintained: location + access + tier are facts no script can derive. The snapshot fields are point-in-time (2026-09-02) and are meant to be regenerated by the consumer-review skill, not edited by hand.

consumers.notes: Local-only git repo, no remote — cannot receive a GitHub PR. Heaviest consumer and the origin of the host-exec/vm/incus module family. ~20 sibling worktrees (foundry-*) plus forge-releases/ snapshots; review the canonical checkout only.
Only consumer pinning @zabaca/zbc in package.json, and it is 3 minors behind (npm latest 0.15.0). Clean subtree, no vendor drift. The `workspace` environment is a third env shape nothing else has.

Largest copy-mode divergence: cloudflare is 734 diff-lines off upstream. The two checkouts have themselves diverged (mac has `obs`, ryzen-9 has `lima-engine`) — reconcile before reviewing. Sole author of gcp/posthog/vercel alongside foothill-metabolic.

Densest Cloudflare surface of any consumer: 12 instances, most of them token/zone/access plumbing. Authors two modules nothing upstream has (cloudflare-access-service-token, cloudflare-account-member).

Only consumer besides zbc itself running the inbox app template (foothill-inbox, foothill-inbox-raw, foothill-inbox-auth-db). Its cloudflare copy is a 249-line fork of a 574-line upstream — an old ancestor, not a patch.
Local dir name (zabaca-web) does not match the repo name (web).
Clean subtree consumer of the host-exec/vm family — the control case against foundry, which needed 13 of its own modules for the same environment shape.

Local-only git repo, no remote. No environments or instances at all — pure module authoring. A per-client provisioning layer built on top of zbc; the strongest evidence for whatever composition primitive zbc is missing.
Public repo. Smallest real consumer — good canary for whether an upgrade path works without inside knowledge.
Clean subtree, no vendor drift, vendored at the same squash as cedarpad (d4cb29d). Empty preview environment.
Public repo. Thinnest copy-mode consumer: one drifted module, one instance. Cheapest subtree-migration pilot.
zbc itself, live consumer of its own templates via symlink. Baseline for every drift measurement, never a PR target.
